- **Static electricity, conductors and insulators, Leyden jar** [`static_electricity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/static_electricity.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. Rubbed amber and jet drawing chaff is a curiosity from Pliny and Albertus Magnus, lumped with the lodestone. Sulphur, glass, silk and beaten gold are on sale. Local: apothecaries (sulphur); makers of amber rosary beads; goldbeaters.
- **Lightning rod** [`lightning_rod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lightning_rod.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Lightning is God's sign or the work of demons in the air; church bells are rung against storms. A rod on a tower is cheap but suspicious. Local: tower of the Palazzo dei Priori; the unfinished campanile.
- **Electric battery (voltaic pile)** [`electric_battery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/electric_battery.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Metallic zinc is unknown in Europe (only calamine, for brass). Copper-iron or silver-iron piles in brine or vinegar work, but weakly. Local: coppersmiths; goldsmiths. Elsewhere: India (Zawar), zinc smelting.
- **Constant and rechargeable cells (Daniell, lead-acid, dry cell)** [`practical_batteries`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/practical_batteries.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Blue vitriol, lead and unglazed pots are available; zinc is not, and oil of vitriol is a rarity of alchemists.
